title: Closure of UL under complement
formal:
Is unambiguous logarithmic space closed under Boolean complement?
\[\forall L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*,\qquad L\in\mathrm{UL}\ \Longrightarrow\ \{0,1\}^*\setminus L\in\mathrm{UL}.\]
Equivalently, is \(\mathrm{UL}=\mathrm{coUL}\)? A language is in \(\mathrm{UL}\) if one uniform nondeterministic machine decides it using logarithmic work space and has at most one accepting computation path on every input.

The complementing machine must also have at most one accepting path on every input and logarithmic space with its own fixed constants. The question concerns ordinary uniform machines with no advice or oracle and arbitrary binary input languages, not only planar graph problems.

why: Unambiguity retains existential computation while limiting each positive instance to a unique accepting history. Complement closure asks whether the same economy is available for negative instances. Its resolution would clarify a basic structural property between deterministic and nondeterministic logarithmic space and the interpretation and composition of functions computed using unambiguous subroutines.

importance.reason: A central closure question for a longstanding small-space complexity class, connected to the NL-versus-UL conjecture and to the foundations of unambiguous graph algorithms and function composition.
importance.basis: Individual assessment of the universal class-comparison target, its standard complementation contrast and documented algorithmic consequences.

sentences: UL contains languages decided with logarithmic work space and at most one accepting computation path per input.
The question asks whether the complement of every such language also has an unambiguous logarithmic-space decider.
The original and complement machines are uniform, exact and have no oracle or nonuniform advice.
Ordinary nondeterministic logspace is closed under complement, but its complementing procedures need not preserve unambiguity.
A resolution would clarify both the structure of small-space complexity classes and the use of unambiguous subroutines in graph algorithms.

definitions:
A language is any set of finite binary strings, and \(n=|x|\) denotes input length. Use a nondeterministic multitape Turing machine with fixed finite control and fixed finite tape alphabets, a two-way read-only input tape with end markers, and finitely many initially blank work tapes. Each transition has at most two choices. The input cannot be modified or used as additional writable memory. Work space is the total number of work-tape cells visited along a computation, measured in bits up to the fixed alphabet factor; the input cells and fixed finite control are not charged as work space.

A machine is logarithmic-space bounded if there is a constant \(c\) such that every computation on every input of length \(n\) visits at most \(c\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) work cells. Use the standard halting convention: some fixed polynomial \(K(n+2)^d\) bounds the number of steps along every computation path, including rejecting paths. The machine and \(c,K,d\) are fixed independently of the input. A polynomial clock fits in logarithmic space; this convention does not add a nonuniform resource.

A computation path is a complete sequence of transition choices from the initial configuration to an accepting or rejecting halt. Distinct choice histories count as distinct paths even when they later reach the same configuration. Acceptance means that at least one path accepts. The machine decides \(L\) when it accepts exactly the strings of \(L\); all paths on strings outside \(L\) reject.

Unambiguity means at most one accepting path for every binary input. Therefore a yes-instance has exactly one accepting path, while a no-instance has none. There may be many rejecting paths in either case. No probability distribution or bounded-error interpretation of these paths is intended. This is not the stronger requirement that every configuration, or every pair of configurations, be connected by at most one path.

The class \(\mathrm{UL}\) consists of languages decided by some machine satisfying all these conditions. Define \(\mathrm{coUL}=\{\overline L:L\in\mathrm{UL}\}\), where \(\overline L=\{0,1\}^*\setminus L\). Dropping only the unambiguity restriction gives \(\mathrm{NL}\), and restricting to deterministic transitions gives \(\mathrm L\). The usual inclusions are \(\mathrm L\subseteq\mathrm{UL}\subseteq\mathrm{NL}\). The known closure \(\mathrm{NL}=\mathrm{coNL}\) makes \(\mathrm{UL}=\mathrm{NL}\) sufficient for the requested closure; no equivalence to that stronger equality is asserted.

The quantifier is over languages: for each language with a qualifying machine, another qualifying machine for its complement must exist. An effective compiler that transforms every description of an unambiguous machine into a complement machine is not additionally required. Nor must the original and complement machines have the same space constant or polynomial clock. A negative answer is a language in \(\mathrm{UL}\) whose complement is not in \(\mathrm{UL}\), with nonmembership excluding all possible unambiguous logarithmic-space machines.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of closure in the declared uniform model. A proof must establish a qualifying complement machine for every language in UL, with exact acceptance, unambiguity on all inputs and logarithmic work space. A refutation must establish a language in UL and prove that its complement has no such machine. Merely complementing nondeterministic logspace while allowing multiple accepting paths, adding advice or an oracle, or settling a restricted family of graph inputs does not meet the full criterion. An oracle separation or a conditional separation alone is not an unconditional refutation.

context_blocks.text: The source explicitly distinguishes UL from its intersection with coUL when defining functions computed using unambiguous subroutines. Its convenient oracle, circuit and bit-graph descriptions agree for that intersection, whereas general UL complementation is still an open premise.
Nondeterministic space at least logarithmic is known to be closed under complement. The theorem permits several accepting histories, so it does not alone give an unambiguous complement machine.

The 2026 long-path paper obtains new parameterized algorithms and states separate unambiguous and co-unambiguous guarantees for one resource bound. Such results concern a specified graph task and its parameter; they do not establish closure for every UL language. Only its abstract and stated resource scope were used in this status check.
